rationale: Corrected the healed-partition fact: its statement said the restarted side ended as a follower at term 4, which came from construction-time feedback, while the retained receipt records the opposite direction — in the flag-enabled case the restarted side was the one Leader at term 4 with the other side's committed entry still present, and only the flag-disabled control ended with the restarted side a follower at term 3. The substantive observation (one leader after healing, both divergent committed entries still present) is unchanged and does not depend on which side wins; the entry now states the receipt's operands and records that the direction varied between local feedback and the retained run.

knowledge.statement: In the retained healed-partition execution the cluster converged on leadership but not on content: after the connections were restored it held exactly one leader (leaders_after_heal 1, parsed index 49) and that leader was the restarted side, at term 4, yet both divergent committed entries were still present, the restarted side's own entry in its store and the other side's entry in theirs (first_entry_survives true, second_entry_survives true, entries_surviving 2); the flag-disabled control ended with one leader as well, the restarted side a follower at term 3 and only the entry that had been committed there (entries_surviving 1 at parsed index 52). The two entries had been written at the same index while both sides held the same term, so each side's AppendEntries treats the other's entry as a duplicate rather than a conflict.
knowledge.conditions: The two sides of the partition case had each led and committed one uniquely named entry, as recorded by the split_result event at parsed index 48 of the same run; healing reconnects the restarted side and the two peers in both directions with the transport's Connect, waits twice the 800 ms election window and then searches each store for the two payload strings. The observation covers log-store contents and leadership only; which side wins the post-heal election varied between construction-time feedback (the restarted side a follower) and the retained run (the restarted side the leader), and the surviving divergence does not depend on that direction.
knowledge.changed_premise: The earlier revision of this fact recorded the restarted side as a follower at term 4, taken from construction-time feedback rather than from the retained receipt. The retained execution shows the opposite direction for the flag-enabled case, with the restarted side the single leader at term 4 and the other side's entry still in its store, and the control as a follower at term 3. The count of surviving divergent entries, which is the substantive claim, is unchanged.
